sentences.text: The Statue of Liberty -LRB- Liberty Enlightening the World ; -LSB- La Liberté éclairant le monde , links = no -RSB- -RRB- is a colossal neoclassical sculpture on Liberty Island in New York Harbor in New York City , in the United States .	Liberty Island	Liberty Island	New York Harbor	New York Harbor	neoclassical sculpture	neoclassical sculpture	New York City	New York City	United States	United States

The copper statue , a gift from the people of France to the people of the United States , was designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi and built by Gustave Eiffel .	Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi	Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi	United States	United States	Gustave Eiffel	Gustave Eiffel
The statue was dedicated on October 28 , 1886 .
The Statue of Liberty is a robed female figure representing Libertas , the Roman goddess .	Libertas	Libertas

She holds a torch above her head , and in her left arm carries a tabula ansata inscribed in Roman numerals with `` JULY IV MDCCLXXVI '' -LRB- July 4 , 1776 -RRB- , the date of the U.S. Declaration of Independence .	tabula ansata	tabula ansata	Roman numerals	Roman numerals	U.S. Declaration of Independence	United States Declaration of Independence
A broken chain lies at her feet .
The statue became an icon of freedom and of the United States , and was a welcoming sight to immigrants arriving from abroad .	United States	United States

Bartholdi was inspired by French law professor and politician Édouard René de Laboulaye , who is said to have commented in 1865 that any monument raised to U.S. independence would properly be a joint project of the French and U.S. peoples .	Édouard René de Laboulaye	Édouard René de Laboulaye
Due to the post-war instability in France , work on the statue did not commence until the early 1870s .	post-war instability in France	History of France#Second Empire, 1852–71
In 1875 , Laboulaye proposed that the French finance the statue and the U.S. would provide the site and build the pedestal .
Bartholdi completed the head and the torch-bearing arm before the statue was fully designed , and these pieces were exhibited for publicity at international expositions .

The torch-bearing arm was displayed at the Centennial Exposition in Philadelphia in 1876 , and in Madison Square Park in Manhattan from 1876 to 1882 .	Manhattan	Manhattan	Centennial Exposition	Centennial Exposition	Madison Square Park	Madison Square Park
Fundraising proved difficult , especially for the Americans , and by 1885 work on the pedestal was threatened due to lack of funds .

Publisher Joseph Pulitzer of the New York World started a drive for donations to complete the project that attracted more than 120,000 contributors , most of whom gave less than a dollar .	Joseph Pulitzer	Joseph Pulitzer	New York World	New York World
The statue was constructed in France , shipped overseas in crates , and assembled on the completed pedestal on what was then called Bedloe 's Island .

The statue 's completion was marked by New York 's first ticker-tape parade and a dedication ceremony presided over by President Grover Cleveland .	ticker-tape parade	ticker-tape parade	Grover Cleveland	Grover Cleveland

The statue was administered by the United States Lighthouse Board until 1901 and then by the Department of War ; since 1933 it has been maintained by the National Park Service .	National Park Service	National Park Service	United States	United States	United States Lighthouse Board	United States Lighthouse Board	Department of War	United States Department of War
Public access to the balcony surrounding the torch has been barred for safety reasons since 1916 .
